title: A way back after three misses
statement: After three misses in a row, a lesson still gives useful correction and a way to recover, never just an answer to copy or a dead end.
detail: The acceptance criteria a Grade 5 reading course set itself before it could be called student-ready include a frustration-recovery probe, which shows what happens after three consecutive misses. The flow passes only if it gives useful correction and a recoverable path, not answer-copying or abandonment. The course's BrainLift sets the same direction for any miss: correction, a parallel check, delayed retest, spaced return and a capped retry, so that a wrong response reopens instruction.
against: A rule on record reveals the answer after two tries so that a student who never gets it right can still finish (two-tries-then-the-answer); a reveal the student simply copies is what this probe rules out, so the two pull against each other.

evidence.quote: - A frustration-recovery probe shows what happens after three consecutive misses: the flow must give useful correction and a recoverable path, not answer-copying or abandonment.
